title: Why Bridges Have Gaps
coreQuestion: Why do bridges have metal gaps you drive over?

facts.claim: An expansion joint is an assembly designed to hold parts together while safely absorbing temperature-induced expansion and contraction of building materials.
Bridge expansion joints are designed to allow continuous traffic between structures while accommodating movement, shrinkage and temperature variations.
Thermal expansion is the tendency of matter to increase in length, area or volume in response to an increase in temperature.

narration.text: Those metal gaps you drive over on a bridge are there on purpose.
They give the bridge room to change size.
Matter grows in size as its temperature rises. That is thermal expansion.
A long deck of steel and concrete grows on a hot day and shrinks on a cold one.
An expansion joint holds the parts together while safely absorbing that movement.
On a bridge, the joint also has to keep traffic moving across it.
The gap is the bridge making room for the weather.
